Faster than you, crazier than you, and more than capable of dicing you up.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Max-Tac).
information.notes:
Threat level: Elite Hardened Boss
Facedown #: 11
COM#: 16

Weapons:

  • Mantis Blade x2 (EQ): ROF 2, 3d6 (Mantis Blade)
  • Spring-Loaded Dual Mantis Blades (EQ) [Has a 4m/yds range w/ Jump Boosters]: ROF 1, 4d6 (Mantis Blade)

Armor:

  • Both have an Ultralight Rebuild.
  • Melee SP (head/body): 8/8

Situational skill values:

  • Athletics 16 (15)
  • Brawling 16 (15)
  • Evasion 15 (14)
  • Martial Arts (Karate) 16 (15)
  • Perception 10 (12)
  • Stealth 14 (13)

Not built:

  • Self-ICE x2 (in Neural Link): from official Cyberpunk RED material by R. Talsorian Games; not in the Cyberpunk RED - Core Foundry system

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.
Throwing hands, does ignore half armor.

Cost: 10,000eb (Super Luxury)

Built for MAX-TAC, this helmet contains the most robust optical suite ever packed into headgear. A fully kitted-out model can locate and track threats in any environment, while its nano-alloy easily resists small arms fire without over-encumbering its user. To put it simply, the Max-Helm’s capabilities are as insane as its users are.

SP 16 Head Armor with an Armor Penalty of -1 to REF, and -2 to DEX and MOVE. All ablation this armor would suffer is reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). This armor’s SP is not halved by Martial Arts Attacks and Special Moves. Has built-in Smart Ears (w/ Level Damper and Radio Communicator) and modified Smart Glasses with 8 Option Slots for Cybereye Options. This armor is also capable of installing Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancements. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of each day in which it does not lose SP.

Covers: Head
SP: 16
Armor Penalty: -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE

Foundry notes:

  • Corgo's penalty is -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE. The sheet applies one penalty to all three stats, so it uses -2; add the difference back by hand for the lighter stat(s).

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Catalog).

Cost: 15,000eb (Super-Luxury)

Rolled out in 2069, this next-gen tactical armor uses flexible materials and crystalline gels for maximum protection at very little weight. Its glowing lines may resemble a fashion statement, but in reality, they’re part of a powered exoshell that can accept external cybernetics such as EMP buffers, dermal reinforcements, or even optical camouflage.

SP 16 Body Armor with an Armor Penalty of -1 to REF, and -2 to DEX and MOVE. All ablation this armor would suffer is reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). This armor’s SP is not halved by Martial Arts Attacks and Special Moves. Has 1 Option Slot for External Body Cyberware, which ignores installation requirements (including being an FBC and required Option Slots), but cannot install cyberware that grants or restores SP.

This armor is also capable of installing Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancements. While worn, the user may access any of the armor’s installed Cyberware, which does not cause any Humanity Loss or consume any of their Cyberware Option Slots. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of a day in which it does not lose SP.

Covers: Body
SP: 16
Armor Penalty: -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE

Foundry notes:

  • Corgo's penalty is -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE. The sheet applies one penalty to all three stats, so it uses -2; add the difference back by hand for the lighter stat(s).

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Catalog).
A cybernetical replacement arm. Comes with a free hand.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 7 (2d6)

Arm blades designed with lethality and concealment in mind. As effective as they are flashy.

Cyberarm/Cyberleg Option. Requires 2 Option Slots. A One-Handed Excellent Quality Heavy Melee Weapon that can be successfully concealed without a Check and can be drawn and stowed without an Action. While the weapon is “popped up,” the user can’t hold anything in this arm’s hand (Cyberlegs do not have this downside, unless they’re currently using a Prehensile Cyberfoot). When purchased twice and installed in two paired Cyberlimbs, the user can negate the normal movement penalty for climbing while both weapons are popped up.

Type: Cyberarm
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 2

Foundry notes:

  • Cyberware items have no Quality field, so the Excellent Quality is in the text only.
  • Corgo allows this in a Cyberleg too; the item is typed as a Cyberarm option, so install it by hand for a leg.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Cyberarms).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

Exceeds legal limits for spring tension to unleash terrifying leaps.

Mantis Blade Cyberware Enhancement. Whenever the Mantis Blade would ablate armor, it ablates 1 additional SP. Additionally, if the user has at least one other installed Mantis Blade with this enhancement, and has paired Jump Boosters or Reinforced Tendons, they may wield both Mantis Blades as a single Excellent Quality Very Heavy Melee Weapon with a 4m/yds range while both weapons are popped up.

Enhances: Mantis Blade
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Teach them to respect your personal space. If they don’t listen, make sure their disrespect doesn’t leave you defenseless.

External Body Cyberware. While installed, the first Attack the user is hit by in a Round from an attacker within 6m/yds has its incoming damage (before interacting with armor) reduced by 1. This cyberware can be installed multiple times, to a maximum of two installations.

Type: External Body Cyberware
Install: Clinic

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > External Body Cyberware).
Access to nervous system.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

The modern Kerenzikov takes the place of the now defunct Reflex Co-Processor to help reduce the strain on the user's Neuroport.

Neuralware. The user can now dodge Ranged Attacks if they could not do so already, and gain a +2 bonus to Checks for noticing Ambushes.

NOTE: Credit to Infernox_Ratchet for the basis of this item.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Kerenzikov; use this one instead of the core item.
  • The +2 is on Perception and situational, because it only applies to noticing an Ambush: tick it in the roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

If you want to stay in the game, you’re going to need a boost.

Kerenzikov Cyberware Enhancement. The Kerenzikov now counts as Speedware and also provides a +2 bonus to initiative at all times. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Enhances: Kerenzikov
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • The +2 initiative isn't automated from an upgrade; add it to the Kerenzikov as an Active Effect (bonuses.initiative) or apply it by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).
Chipware. Removes Seriously Wounded penalties.

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 7 (2d6)

Neuroprocessor that can regulate hormonal balance when needed.

Neuralware. The user may activate this cyberware without an Action to re-roll a Critical Failure (1) they get when rolling Initiative or making a Check with one of the following Skills: Athletics, Concentration, Perception, Stealth. The user must keep the new result, even if it is lower. This cyberware has a 4 hour cooldown before it can be used again. Only one Synaptic Accelerator can be installed.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1
